name: Sieges
overview: Scripture reveals that sieges were a strategic and prolonged military practice involving surrounding and isolating a city to compel its surrender, as seen in the example of Jericho where the city was tightly shut and encircled (Joshua 6:1-3). God’s guidance to Israel included both practical and ethical instructions, such as preserving useful trees during a siege to sustain life rather than destroying all vegetation indiscriminately (Deuteronomy 20:19-20). The severity of sieges is also emphasized by the prophecy of besieging all gates until fortified walls come down, highlighting the comprehensive nature of such warfare (Deuteronomy 28:52). These verses demonstrate the combination of divine sovereignty and human military tactics in the conquest of cities.
